name: A11Y.md Efficacy Benchmark
description: Study 3 of the A11Y.md benchmark line — the v2.0.0 audit. Studies 1–2 measured whether a written accessibility standard (A11Y.md v1.8.0) changes what AI coding agents build, against no-guidance and generic-phrase controls. Their findings drove a revision of the standard itself (v2.0.0). This study registers the before/after as its own primary question: does v2.0.0 improve on v1.8.0, on the same frozen 7-screen bookstore-journey unit, per agent, never pooled? Design: 4 conditions (A: bare; B: "Make it accessible."; D18: the standard at tag v1.8.0; D20: at tag v2.0.0) × 2 agents (Claude Code 2.1.237, Antigravity 1.1.22) × 5 runs = 40 journeys, interleaved collection, sanitized per-agent environments (closed allow-lists, hashed manifests, leakage gate probes passed and journaled). Primary contrast: D20 vs D18, same-agent. Statistical posture: descriptive and estimation-oriented — seeded journey-cluster bootstrap, Cliff's delta, no p-values; at n=5×5 only near-complete separation is distinguishable from noise (null SD of Cliff's delta ≈ 0.38, printed so no reader over-reads). Three pre-declared falsifiable commitments from the v2.0.0 release: non-regression of the token diet (measured per obligation, never as volume); the kill criterion (Study 2's half-climbed ARIA ladder must disappear as a class — binary, with its 2×2 table against D18); and the contrast bet (v2.0.0's deterministic contrast protocol, per-agent corroboration rules declared).
